chain.label: FAA oversight of Marlin Air and of its check airman appointment was inadequate
chain.trigger: the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) failure to detect and correct those deficiencies

chain.label: Ill-prepared first officer cleared by an inadequate company checkride; both pilots lacked systems knowledge
chain.trigger: the inadequate checkrides administered by Marlin Air's chief pilot/check airman ... placed an ill-prepared pilot in the first officer's seat

caused_by.evidence: the POI did not pursue additional information because he did not believe it was necessary

chain.label: Citation design deficiencies: identical adjacent autopilot/yaw damper buttons and hypersensitive unpowered aileron trim
chain.trigger: the design and location of the yaw damper and autopilot switches on Cessna Citation series airplanes do not adequately protect against inadvertent activation ... the Citation 550 aileron trim is highly sensitive and effective

chain.label: Chafed control-column wiring with pre-existing short circuits in the first officer's yoke; Cessna SB 550-24-14 not accomplished
chain.trigger: at least two short circuits occurred in a bundle of wires in the first officer's control yoke/column ... SB 550-24-14 had not been accomplished on the accident airplane

chain.label: Abnormal flight control situation just after takeoff (inadvertent autopilot engagement or runaway pitch trim)
chain.trigger: the accident sequence initiated as a result of a control problem that was related to either an inadvertent autopilot activation or a pitch trim anomaly

caused_by.evidence: inadvertent activation of the autopilot when activation of the yaw damper is intended is not an uncommon occurrence
This short circuit exposed the cores of multiple wires, providing a potential source of power to the pitch trim motor

chain.label: Pilots troubleshot haphazardly and never consulted an abnormal or emergency checklist
chain.trigger: the pilots engaged in a haphazard and confusing troubleshooting process ... neither pilot referenced a checklist for assistance in resolving the control anomaly

caused_by.evidence: why am I fighting the controls here?
both pilots lacked procedural knowledge and familiarity with the airplane's systems

chain.label: First officer made unrequested aileron/rudder trim inputs that worsened the out-of-trim condition
chain.trigger: it is likely that the first officer's trim inputs aggravated, rather than ameliorated, the situation

caused_by.evidence: The disproportionate sensitivity and responsiveness of this system would likely have compounded any aileron trim inputs made by the first officer

chain.label: Captain let the airplane accelerate to about 245 knots instead of reducing power while troubleshooting
chain.trigger: the result would have been controllable if the captain had not allowed the airspeed and resulting control forces to increase while he tried to troubleshoot the problem

caused_by.evidence: if the pilots had simply maintained a reduced airspeed while they responded to the situation, the aerodynamic forces on the airplane would not have increased significantly
The captain allowed the airplane to accelerate and climb after takeoff ... while he and the first officer tried to troubleshoot the control anomaly

chain.label: Uncoordinated crew; captain handed the controls to the ill-prepared first officer to pull circuit breakers
chain.trigger: you hold it, I'm gonna try to pull circuit breakers ... the pilots did not coordinate with each other regarding trim inputs

caused_by.evidence: the first officer provided little help to, and likely hindered, the captain during his attempts to deal with the flight control anomalies
he increasingly struggled as the airplane accelerated and the control forces increased

chain.label: Control forces exceeded what the crew could hold; airplane rolled left into a steep nose-down descent
chain.trigger: we're not...holding it ... almost immediately after the first officer took control, the airplane rolled to the left and descended into the lake

caused_by.evidence: The final loss of control began about 1 minute later, just after the captain transferred the controls to the first officer
without the power reduction, control forces were excessive
the effects of which were compounded by aileron and/or rudder trim inputs

chain.label: Airplane impacted Lake Michigan at about 243 knots in a steep nose-down, left-wing-low attitude
chain.trigger: the airplane impacted Lake Michigan at a speed of about 243 knots, in a steep (about 42 degrees) nose-down, left-wing-low attitude

caused_by.evidence: the airplane rolled to the left and descended into the lake

chain.label: All six occupants fatally injured; airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The two pilots and four passengers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable due to impact forces
